gloss: shrinking back, being fed up, weariness

definitions.gloss: shrinking back, being overwhelmed, being pushed back
definitions.explanation: The state of being pushed back or overwhelmed by something powerful or intense. Originally meant retreating from a superior force.

definitions.gloss: being fed up, being sick of, weariness
definitions.explanation: The state of being tired of or disgusted with something due to excess or persistence. Used when something becomes unbearable.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{勢|いきお}いに{辟易|へきえき}した。
examples.english: I was overwhelmed by his intensity.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}の{迫力|はくりょく}に{辟易|へきえき}して、{後|あと}ずさりした。
examples.english: Overwhelmed by the opponent's force, I stepped back.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{強引|ごういん}さには{誰|だれ}もが{辟易|へきえき}させられた。
examples.english: Everyone was put off by his pushiness.

examples.japanese: {連日|れんじつ}の{暑|あつ}さに{辟易|へきえき}している。
examples.english: I'm fed up with the heat day after day.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{自慢話|じまんばなし}には{辟易|へきえき}する。
{毎日|まいにち}{同|おな}じことの{繰|く}り{返|かえ}しに{辟易|へきえき}していた。
examples.english: I was weary of the same thing repeating every day.

notes:
USAGE: Used with する to form the verb {辟易|へきえき}する. Can also be used as a taru-adjective: {辟易|へきえき}たる{思|おも}い.

NUANCE: {辟易|へきえき} originally meant being pushed back by a powerful force (sense 1), but is now more commonly used to mean being fed up or disgusted (sense 2). Both senses convey being overwhelmed by something.

ETYMOLOGY: From Chinese, originally describing retreating from battle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {辟易|へきえき}する (to be overwhelmed/fed up)
- ～に{辟易|へきえき}する (to be fed up with ~)
- {辟易|へきえき}させる (to put someone off)

RELATED WORDS:
- うんざりする (to be fed up - more casual)
- {閉口|へいこう}する (to be at a loss, fed up)
- {嫌気|いやけ}が{差|さ}す (to be sick of)
